claims.text: The initial particles are equiatomic AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles approximately 5–8 nm in diameter.
The as-synthesized AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are a single-phase solid solution.
Rapid quenching or inert-gas condensation produces the stated initial structure.
The proposed thermal treatment is heating from 300 K to 1000 K at 10 K/min in 10^-6 Torr vacuum.
The vacuum environment prevents oxidation during heating.
Above 600 K, surface-energy effects overwhelm sluggish diffusion in sub-10 nm AuCoCuNiPt particles.
The particles undergo rapid phase separation, including spinodal decomposition, rather than retaining entropy-stabilized homogeneity.
A high surface-to-volume ratio creates a surface-energy gradient that lowers the activation barrier for surface diffusion and atomic exchange.
Surface atomic exchange bypasses the bulk sluggish-diffusion constraint.
Structural evolution above 600 K proceeds by surface-diffusion-limited Ostwald ripening.
Au and Cu are relatively low-surface-energy elements and segregate to particle surfaces or distinct domains.
Pt, Co, and Ni coalesce into larger, compositionally enriched cores.
Surface-driven segregation and ripening are faster than configurational-entropy-driven mixing.
Particles smaller than 5 nm are preferentially lost through dissolution or evaporation of surface atoms.
Material from the smallest particles contributes to the growth of larger particles.
Heating produces a Pt/Ni-rich core and an Au/Cu-rich shell or separate Au-rich and Pt-rich domains.
High configurational entropy can stabilize equiatomic multielement solid solutions and HEAs are commonly associated with sluggish diffusion and thermal stability.
Configurational entropy would maintain homogeneous AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles without significant growth or phase separation up to 1000 K.
For particles larger than 20 nm, bulk sluggish diffusion may dominate and preserve homogeneity longer.
Heating below 1 K/min may permit equilibrium thermodynamic stabilization, while reactive atmospheres may change the pathway by altering surface energies.

contradictions.description: The initial state is specified as single phase, but the predicted outcome describes phase separation while also claiming a significant reduction in the number of distinct phases. Relative to a single-phase starting state, separation into Au-rich and Pt-rich domains would increase, not reduce, the number of phases.
